title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: Charges Raised at Approval and at Loading
content:
## Clause

Dangerous Goods Acceptance charges fall at two moments. Each approval brings the category's administration fee. The surcharges fall at loading, that is, when the goods are actually carried.

At loading, a single hazardous-cargo surcharge entry is written for the acceptance. Its per-container base is the category's 20-foot rate for 20-foot units and its 40-foot rate for 40-foot and 45-foot units. That base is raised by the sum of three uplift percentages — the uplift for the declared class, the packing-group I uplift where the packing group is I, and the uplift for the booking's trade lane — which are added to one another and never compounded. Where the customer has a service contract in active status and the rank of its tier reaches the category's minimum qualifying rank, the uplifted figure is then reduced by the category's contract discount percentage; a minimum rank of 0 means no discount is given. The per-container figure multiplied by the containers of the acceptance, rounded to the cent, is the surcharge; the surcharge falls to 0.00 for an acceptance whose gross weight lies below the category's surcharge-free weight.

Goods marked as marine pollutant carry a second entry at loading: the category's marine-pollutant rate per container multiplied by the containers.

## Conditions on booking these charges

- Surcharges may be entered only on an acceptance whose status is approved or loaded.
- For each charge code, one entry per charging date; the account entries of the acceptance show whether a code has already been charged on that date.

## Which entries arise when

| Moment | Entry | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| Approval | administration fee | every approval |
| Loading | hazardous-cargo surcharge | once for the acceptance; 0.00 below the surcharge-free weight |
| Loading | marine-pollutant surcharge | only for goods marked marine pollutant |

## Points of judgement

**Does the packing-group uplift apply to packing group II?** No; it is added only when the packing group is I, and counts as nil otherwise.

**Is a heavy acceptance ever exempt?** The exemption concerns acceptances whose gross weight is below the surcharge-free weight; an acceptance at or above that weight pays the surcharge.
